title: The Quiz Wife
logline: The gang discovers that Robin and Marshall have spent thirty-one Wednesdays secretly winning pub quiz at another bar as Team Polar Vortex, and it plays exactly like an affair. Ted, Lily and Barney demand a rematch and cram with a solo rival who has finished second thirty-one weeks running, while Lily's lasagna bribe puts Marshall between his wife and his quiz wife.
coldOpen: Kids, in the spring of 2012, your Aunt Robin and your Uncle Marshall had a secret. Every Wednesday night for thirty-one weeks, they snuck off together to another bar. And they were very, very good together.

couch.line: Dad. Did Uncle Marshall cheat on Aunt Lily with Aunt Robin?
What? No. Kids, it was a pub quiz.
Luke, there were stakes. A twenty-dollar bar tab, and our entire friendship.

guests.name: Lorne Pruitt
guests.role: Quizmaster at the Wobbly Owl for twenty-two years and a retired police hostage negotiator; runs trivia in a calm, soothing crisis voice, talks contestants down from wrong answers, and fines anyone who says 'technically' five points

guests.name: Gail Pomeroy
guests.role: A retired reference librarian who competes alone as Team Gail, has finished second to Polar Vortex thirty-one weeks running, keeps a scouting file on every team, shushes anyone above a murmur, and flirts, if at all, in pure facts

scenes.summary: Wednesday, eleven-fifteen. Lily is suspicious of Marshall's 'Minnesota support group'. Robin and Marshall arrive in matching hoodies with mismatched excuses. Lily reads Marshall's texts: a lightning round. It's exactly what it looks like, but with trivia: Team Polar Vortex, thirty-one and oh. Lily: he has a quiz wife. Ted the trivia guy wasn't wanted (the 'technically' rule, runner 1); Barney wasn't even considered (flashback: 'Barney?' 'Barney.'). Lily demands a rematch. Carl knew all along: nachos are down.

beats.line: It was a Wednesday. Robin and Marshall were late. Again.
Eleven-fifteen. Marshall said his Minnesota support group ends at nine.
Lily, there's no Minnesota support group in New York.
That's what I said. He said that's because nobody wants to be a bother.
Every Wednesday, a fake support group. Lily, I invented that move. Mine was for people who'd lost a twin.
Why are you two wearing the same hoodie?
Dentist.
Work thing.
Work thing.
Dentist.
Marshall. Phone. Now.

messages.text: No, you were. That lightning round!

beats.line: Lightning round? What is a lightning round, Marshall?
Marshall. A lightning round. I didn't know you had it in you.
Lilypad, it's not what it looks like.
What does it look like?
Like Robin and I sneak off to a dark bar every Wednesday, sit at a tiny table for two, and whisper.
Okay, it's exactly what it looks like. But with trivia.
Pub quiz. The Wobbly Owl, on Ninth. We're a team.
Team Polar Vortex. Thirty-one wins, zero losses.
Oh my God. You have a quiz wife.
Pub quiz. Without me. Robin, I'm the trivia guy. I own a first-edition almanac.
Ted, that's why.
Buddy, the Wobbly Owl has one rule. Anyone who says technically loses five points.
That's absurd. Technically, technically is the most important word in trivia.
Ten points.
How are you two even good? You don't have anything in common.
Ted, Robin knows what happened. I know what really happened.
He's cost us points on the moon landing twice.
Fine. You didn't want Ted. Nobody wants Ted. But you didn't even consider me?
Barney, we considered you!
We did. We had a whole conversation about it.

beats.label: The Wobbly Owl, thirty-one weeks ago

beats.line: Should we ask Barney to join?
Barney?
Barney.
Polar Vortex?
Love it.
That's not considering! That's saying my name twice and then naming your team!
Fine. Next Wednesday. Polar Vortex against the real team. Me, Ted and Barney.
Bring tissues, Lily. Last week we made a Columbia professor cry on the hockey round.
Challenge accepted.
Ted. Quick question. Is Australia a country or a continent?
Both.
Challenge still accepted.
Carl! They've been going to another bar!
I know.
How?
Wednesday nachos are down.

scenes.summary: The real team's cram session. Lily's ringer is Gail, who has come second to Polar Vortex thirty-one weeks in a row and has a chart: their only blind spots are art, architecture and Broadway, one lane each. The team name is three names. Ted can't stop saying technically (runner 2, minus forty-five before they start). Barney attaches a pickup line to every answer; Gail answers his octopus line with a fact that floors him. Lily nails art, then admits she's told Marshall the entire strategy for pancakes. Plan B is lasagna. Gail predicts the result.

beats.line: That Sunday, the real team held its first cram session. It went great.
Okay. I brought in a ringer. She's come second to Polar Vortex thirty-one weeks in a row.
Gail. Team Gail. It's just me.
A team of one. Gail, that's either very sad or very hot.
Shh.
I've kept a file on Polar Vortex since week one. Thirty-one weeks of losing teaches you things.
Hockey, food, unsolved mysteries: perfect. Art, architecture and Broadway: helpless.
beats.title: Polar Vortex: Points by Category

beats.line: Art.
Architecture.
Broadway. Tell no one.
Team name?
The Flying Buttresses.
Team Legendary.
Revenge.
Pick one.
No.
Architecture. Who designed the Guggenheim Museum in New York?
Frank Lloyd Wright. Although technically, the spiral was first sketched as a parking—
Minus five! That's nine tonight, Ted. We're at minus forty-five and we haven't started.
I can't help it, Lily. Being right is a reflex.
Broadway. Longest-running show in Broadway history?
The Phantom of the Opera. Fun fact, the chandelier weighs a ton. Much like the tension between us right now.
Correct. Shh.
Octopus. How many hearts?
Three. And all of them are beating for you, Gail.
One of them stops when it swims.
Ted. That's the most beautiful thing anyone's ever said to me.
Art. Who painted The Persistence of Memory?
Dalí. Nineteen thirty-one. Melting clocks. Next.
Finally. A professional.
Most important rule. Polar Vortex can never learn our strategy.
Define learn.
Lily. What did you tell him?
Everything! The categories, the name, Barney's Broadway thing! He made pancakes, Ted. With little faces!
You told him about Broadway?
Relax. I have a Plan B.
What's Plan B?
Lasagna.
Thirty-one weeks, I've come in second.
And with our help, you could finally—
Wednesday, I come in second. You come in third. It'll be the best night of my life.
Ted. She's going to destroy us. I think I'm in love.

scenes.summary: Wednesday, on the C train. Polar Vortex's pre-quiz drill shows how they click: she gets the points, he gets the truth. Marshall leaked back what Lily leaked: art, architecture, Broadway. Robin has Barney's Broadway covered. Then Lily's lasagna text, with a fourth cheese. Marshall might throw one question, a Delaware question. Robin: she's your wife, I'm your quiz wife. Pick a wife. Can he pick after the quiz?

beats.line: Wednesday night, Polar Vortex took the C train to the Wobbly Owl, the way they always did.
Great Lakes.
Superior, Michigan, Huron, Erie, Ontario.
Most penalty minutes, one NHL season.
Dave Schultz. Four seventy-two. Philadelphia. And he deserved every one.
What's in Area Fifty-One?
Aliens.
An Air Force base.
Robin, that's just the answer they give points for.
That is the definition of the right answer.
Lily told me everything. I didn't even ask. I was just making pancakes. Art, architecture, Broadway.
I've got Broadway.
Since when do you know Broadway?
Barney hums Les Mis when he's nervous. I've slept with that man. I know the whole second act.
Robin. She's offering the lasagna.
beats.title: Lilypad

messages.text: Miss one question tonight. Just one.

beats.line: The three-cheese one?
She added a fourth cheese, Robin. She has never added a fourth cheese.
Marshall. Are you going to throw a question?
No! Maybe one. A tiny one. A Delaware question. Nobody cares about Delaware.
Thirty-one weeks, Marshall. Nobody throws a question in Polar Vortex.
Robin, she's my wife!
And I'm your quiz wife!
Pick a wife, Marshall.
Can I pick after the quiz?

scenes.summary: The Wobbly Owl. Lorne the hostage-negotiator quizmaster announces the Flying Buttresses of Legendary Revenge three points ahead, because Polar Vortex missed the Delaware question. Lasagna. Final question: the Minnesota state muffin, which everyone knows. Lily goes over, and Robin and Marshall explain why they hid it: at MacLaren's their homes are punchlines, and they were the only two at the booth without a story of their own. Lily: the most beautiful affair she's ever heard of. Lily tells Ted to say it. Ted throws the game the only way he knows how (runner 3: minus fifteen). Polar Vortex wins, Gail is second, the real team is third, exactly as predicted. Robin knows. Marshall gets one-cheese lasagna. Future Ted: Barney finally got considered, in 2014.

beats.line: I want to hate this place, Lily. But look at that crown molding.
Good evening. Pencils down. Hands where I can see them. Nobody has to get hurt tonight.
After seven rounds. Polar Vortex, seventy. Team Gail, sixty-four.
And our new team, the Flying Buttresses of Legendary Revenge. Seventy-three.
We compromised.
Polar Vortex, you missed one tonight. Round four. Delaware.
Marshall.
It's a really small state, Robin!
Lasagna!
Final question. Ten points. Everybody breathe. What is the official state muffin of Minnesota?
Robin. It's a muffin question. From home.
Blueberry. He orders one at every diner and tells the waitress why.
Ted, we're three up and we know the answer. Is this what winning honestly feels like? It's gross.
Sixty seconds. If anybody feels like making a bad decision, you talk to me first.
You threw a question. For me.
For the fourth cheese. But mostly you.
Thirty-one Wednesdays. Why didn't you just tell us?
Because at MacLaren's, every time I mention Minnesota, somebody does the accent.
Oh, ya, you betcha.
Here, nobody does the accent. Here, Canada is worth ten points. Same as France.
And every two people in that booth have a story. Ted and me. Barney and me. You two. Ted and Marshall.
Robin and I never had one. No breakup, no road trip, no dorm room.
So we got one. And we wanted it to be ours for a while before you guys made it a thing.
That is the most beautiful affair I have ever heard of.
Ted. Say it.
Say what?
You know what.
I have waited my whole life for someone to ask me that.
Lorne! Technically, the blueberry muffin wasn't adopted until nineteen eighty-eight, so technically—
Sir. Put the technically down. Minus ten.
Ted! We were winning!
Technically, we still—
Fifteen.
Final scores. Polar Vortex, eighty. Team Gail, seventy-four. The Flying Buttresses of Legendary Revenge, sixty-eight.
Second. You came third. Best night of my life.
Ted. Did you just throw that?
Technically—
Don't. Thirty-two and oh.
Lilypad. Do I still get the lasagna?
You threw Delaware. You get Delaware lasagna.
What's Delaware lasagna?
One cheese.
Kids, Polar Vortex stayed undefeated for three more years. They lost once, in 2014, when Marshall had the flu and Robin finally considered Barney.
He answered every question with a pickup line. They came in second, to Gail. Barney went home with first place.
